[Update on Paolo](https://stacker.news/items/1613926/r/bief57)
[Update on Paolo II](https://stacker.news/items/1615736/r/bief57)

Photo from last night:

Hahaha, look at how comfortable he is.

Who would’ve thought that the little cat abandoned in the parking lot would end up being so pampered by SN?

![](https://m.stacker.news/167546)

![](https://m.stacker.news/167547)

He has already received 2 doses of dewormer; the next one is due on Wednesday, and then another one 7 days after that third dose.

There are 5 days left in the treatment with the eye drops; by far the best way to do this is to wrap him in a sheet or blanket while one person holds him, and the other person applies the drops.

The issue with his/her loose stools is still giving me a headache. It has been a week since the treatment began; there was significant improvement during the first two days, but then things went back to how they were before. He/she has been given a dewormer, probiotics, and an antifungal, yet his/her stomach remains the same.

The subject of pet nutrition might seem simple, but it is actually quite complex. There is a great deal of conflicting information: some people fully endorse high-quality dry food though, of course, there are lower-quality options that contain more fillers (flours) than actual protein arguing that homemade diets may fail to provide all the essential nutrients a cat needs, such as taurine. Others, by contrast, advocate exclusively for homemade food, claiming that commercial dry or canned cat foods are actually harmful to cats.

Yesterday, I made a homemade pâté for him. I boiled a whole chicken though it didn’t include any giblets along with half a carrot. Once it cooled, I removed all the meat, discarded the bones, and blended the meat and carrot with a little of the water the chicken had been boiled in. He loved it and ate it with great enthusiasm; next time, I’ll buy some extra giblets, like liver and heart, to add to the mix.

![](https://m.stacker.news/167554)

![](https://m.stacker.news/167555)

His gastrointestinal issue needs to improve so that he can receive the remaining vaccine and subsequently be neutered.

items.title: Burning Electricity for Yet More Sats: 21 Energy and their new Ofen 3 Pro
items.text:
*Alternative title:* “3,000 sats a day keeps the doctor away.” *We’re all heatpunks now*!

I hinted at this *a little* already... (https://stacker.news/items/1611882?commentId=1612301, https://stacker.news/items/1613701?commentId=1613729, https://stacker.news/items/1530104)... and finally, today is the day: 

**3,000 words on what it's like to earn 3,000 sats a day.**

In April I posted “[Burning Electricity for 115,000 sats](https://stacker.news/items/1466211)” recapping the experience of having run the Ofen 2 for a few months during winter. For this season, the 21 Energy team graciously sent me their [newest machine](https://21energy.com/products/ofen-3?variant=60451037610318) for review: the **Ofen 3 Pro**.

([Black Week party](https://21energy.com/collections/sales) over there for the next two weeks with *nice juicy prices* if you’re in the market for a home miner! Rivaling [America’s Heatbit](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/business/heat-your-home-while-earning-bitcoin-with-heatbit "https://bitcoinmagazine.com/business/heat-your-home-while-earning-bitcoin-with-heatbit") and the [recent launch](https://www.youtube.com/post/UgkxrtV48gyqN4mygV9xisDudvb_f1b-BrE5 "https://www.youtube.com/post/UgkxrtV48gyqN4mygV9xisDudvb_f1b-BrE5") of its water heater, 21 Energy also just launched a full central heating system called [Focavo](https://21energy.com/de/pages/central-heating). Looks impressive!)

Largely boosted by the recent -9% difficulty adjustment — another metric that normal Bitcoiners don’t care much for but makes miners’ and heatpunks’ eyes go *ka-ching!* — I [breached 3,000 sats](https://x.com/joakimbook/status/2122652928636825847) on a (daily) payout for the first time. That was cool and unexpected.

**Agenda**:

* *User Experience*: what it’s like to use the Ofen 3 Pro (including pics and comparisons to Ofen 2)
* *Raw Numbers:* with all the juicy deets — speaking db, kWh, hashprice, J/TH etc etc
* *The Economic Case for Home Miners*: Returns, and Diminishing Returns
* *Financialization* of Now vs Later

***

## The Glorious User Experience: PICS OR DIDN'T HAPPEN!

This is what we're talking about:

![](https://m.stacker.news/168156)

It's **a machine that eats electricity and spits out heat and sats.** *Simple as that.*

I’ve always found these machines astonishingly beautiful. (Even the Ofen 1, which was a coffee-table type stand, *made me drool in envy!*)
Nothing like the sad, ugly, dusty, worn-out, and plastic-covered electrical heaters that I’m used to in my house.

When you set up the Ofen (both 2 and 3) and it starts hashing, it’s like the fans, firmware, and the ASICs inside need to learn *how* to run at each level. It takes a few days and a few tries for the machine to “get it” at every level. I remember this from my first product, thinking it was broken: *Every time* I would change the settings (from Two to Three, or Three to Four, or Four to One), it would restart itself.

...And if you’ve ever toyed around with any sort of miner, restarting means *loud, crazy fan noises* for an unpredictable while. (Chips gotta cool; machinery gotta clear; the ghost in the machines do their thing.) More than once has this sort of restarting — even after an unannounced firmware too early in the morning — woken me up to incessant fan noises in the next room.

*Oh. This is a good moment to explain how the app that controls the machines works.*

It’s a sleek, green-themed app with five levels that I’ll just call **One**, **Two**, **Three**, **Four** — and **Rocket**. It’s pretty simple, very beautiful, and the machines come with a thermostat that records ambient temperature inside. I don’t really use the thermostat function much (that automatically increases or decreases the hashing to keep a specific temperature) but prefer to manually adjust whenever I feel like they’re too loud for the occasion; I’m outside or it’s cold; or the hashprice is good etc etc.

The inside temperature of my house depends quite a lot on the outdoor weather condition (wind, surprisingly, is more important than temperature) so I just turn the machines up/down whenever it’s appropriate.

![](https://m.stacker.news/168155)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168163)

App interface is very simple, and my only complaint has been a handful of times when turning the Ofen 2 on and off, the app has “frozen” in off mode for days at a time. No way to *manually* or *physically* turn the machine on: there's no "On" button. (To turn it *off*, I can just asymmetrically pull the cord…)

I’ll highlight some of the differences here between the upgraded Ofen 3 Pro and the previous generation, even though the Ofen 2 (or that desirable table stand) is no longer for sale... in case someone is considering whether the upgrade is worth it, etc:

1. **The weight**. It’s significantly lighter, to the point where it (almost) feels like the Ofen 3 seems less sturdy than the original one. Delicate even. The company reps told me about a *third* less heavy (17 kg vs 25 kg for the prev one).
2. **The fan setup**. From the back, the air intake is completely different: two visible fans instead of the larger grid-type filter on the back of the Ofen 2.
3. **Fewer screws**. Way fewer (compare the back side of the machines in the images). Quite possibly why the metal (aluminium?) feels like it's holding itself together less.
4. **Sound:** feels slightly different — lighter or higher-pitched, somehow — and measuring them running on the same level, e.g., Two, they both register 42 dB a feet in front of them but the old one shows 36 dB from the middle of the room, whereas the Ofen 3 Pro shows 32 dB from a distance. (Might depend on the echoes of the room: I didn’t swap the Ofens to double-check; more on noise below.)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168157)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168158)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168159)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168160)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168161)

![](https://m.stacker.news/168162)

***Running Bitcoin miners:***

It’ll take you longer to fiddle with the pool settings than to get the stand screwed on and the electric cord plugged in. **Actually, your biggest trouble is deciding *where* in the house to place the miner.** I was a little concerned about where I might blow a fuse at the highest levels, and also wondered about the fan noise propagating through the house at various times of day.

21 Energy headlines the Ofen 3 for *top* hashing at 60 TH/s, drawing 1100 W.  I learned from the first machine that nobody but a pure psychopath wants to run them at peak effect for longer than a one-time experiment. *Too loud, too inefficient.*

Turning on the Rocket level this morning (just to try and to do my duties and provide the stackers with some raw numbers), the fan spun up markedly from the already loud Four. My measuring device said **it pulled *at the very most* 1278 W… *scheisse* ... but then settled down on a regular 1180W or so.** At first, it pulled that *while* cycling lower into the 40s and 30s TH/s, before going higher — standard miner behavior when switching pace.

I expected the efficiency to trail off markedly, as it does/did with my Ofen 2 at higher settings, but for the Ofen 3 Pro it stayed fairly intact: at *max* effect, which I clocked at **63.7 TH/s** (only caught the screenshot a moment after that one upwick), it remained at around 19 J/TH, astonishingly enough.

Also, that is a pretty good example of how *switching* between the levels is costly (“slippage”) in the efficiency department… it takes a while (sometimes upward of half-an-hour) for the miner to get to its optimal hashing level.

Glad to know my fuses can take that, in case it gets *really cold and stormy* and I want to squeeze out every last drop of hashing heat. The noise from the highest setting was orders of magnitude worse: 47dB in the middle of the room (57dB right in front of the miner), which is a pretty good indicator of how rarely I will use this elevated setting: *never*.

Speaking less numerically about the sound level, on One and Two it’s barely noticeable: **the low murmur of the fans drowns into the background noise**. I live in an exceedingly quiet place, so I imagine anyone in a city, with ambient noise or people and neighbors or birds chirping, will barely even notice this. I keep the Ofen 3 Pro in the living room, separated from my bedroom by a thin door (and somewhat sturdier wall); unless there’s a storm outside, I won’t run it higher than Two or Three at night.
(I would *never* have one of these machines in my bedroom: I’m extremely sensitive to nighttime sounds and selective about what goes there.)

**On Three, the Ofen 3 Pro gives out about 44 TH/s (\~830 W), and it strikes a reasonable trade-off between background noise and heat, comfortably heating a large living room to above 70°F at outdoor temperatures of around freezing.**

…and I learned exactly how much of a difference this makes just the other day, when the outdoor temperature overnight went from freezing, or low-30s, to 42°F... I woke up that morning to the living room and the office both at a boiling 77°F. *Dont need that much heat!*

As I’m writing this, I’m in shorts and t-shirt in the office (24.1°C, 75°F) with nothing but the Ofen 2 in here, running Two and giving off \~24 TH/s. (When I took the screenshot above, I had turned it off... too warm.) In the living room, where the Ofen 3 sits, the app says 22.8°C (73°F) and I’ve had it on Two for 32 TH/s for most of the afternoon.

## The Raw Numbers

Everybody knows that you can’t rely on a company’s headline, on-paper numbers. Not that they intentionally *lie* (one hopes...), but that they might have run the machines in ideal conditions and taken the best numbers, rather than the average or typical uses in the wild.

Similarly, I can’t know if my specific chips are good, bad, extreme, or average compared to other Ofen 2/3 products: **All I can do is report what *these ones* give off.**

For most of this year when I’ve been running the Ofen 2 (on Two or Three mostly) and measuring it, its efficiency has hit *about* 21 J/TH, sometimes, during long stretches, it’s reliably come down to the lower 20s: 20.2, 20.5. At the **18-19.5** that I’m getting with the new Ofen 3 Pro, it’s *nowhere near the 25% better efficiency* the company advertises... but still a decent improvement overall (7%-15%).

All-time payouts from the pool amount to over **400,000 sats**, which feels pretty awesome. (I also have a tiny [Braiins Mini Miner](https://x.com/joakimbook/status/2123404937988334076), running around the clock at \~40W and giving me the lordly hashrate of 1 TH/s; I’ve had this since well before the 21 Energy products, so it skews the total pool numbers a bit.) Depending on difficulty adjustments/how much other hashrate there’s on the network, I’ve been regularly getting daily payouts of about **1,300 sats.**

The Ofen 2 for its first year, had an uptime of probably 90%: I only ever turned it off on extremely warm and sunny spring/summer days, with the sun basking my living room and office and turning it into a tomato-growing Icelandic greenhouse. That’s the *main* [advantage I have](https://youtu.be/2-txiZKNIRk?si=w0Kiri18AxJmTSF9&t=180) as a home miner: Compared to most other (home) miners, **I can usefully run my machines for more hours out of the day, for more days out of the year.**

Since the Ofen 3 Pro arrived about two weeks ago, I’ve run it nonstop. (Fair enough, we’ve had [snowy winter](https://primal.net/e/nevent1qqs8596gxdn9qv8fr6am9zt902jkmff89ajlvy9szc27gkcuf6c9t5s6hee9l) with freezing temperatures this entire time.) Boosted by the [recent hashrate downturn](https://x.com/joakimbook/status/2122652928636825847), I’ve routinely had payouts of 2,700-3,000 sats… *that’s a neat little set-and-forget DCA.*

With *all* taxes and distribution fees included, my per-kWh expense comes out to about $0.17, most of which is tribute to the governmental mafiosos that run this place. (It would be about $0.15 at the more “normal” dollar FX rates we had before “Liberation Day.”) That’s not exactly cheap: Many [places in America](https://www.electricchoice.com/electricity-prices-by-state/) can bag better deals than that, but it’s not awful either. And much better than most places in Scandinavia, *tons* better than mainland Europe — something like half or one-third of residential electricity in Austria or Germany, two places having *tons of fun, staying electricity-poor.*

With today’s hashprice of [$0.03/TH/day](https://data.hashrateindex.com/bitcoin-compute-data/bitcoin-hashprice-index), and assuming I shove something like 65 TH/s/day on average onto the network from my three machines, my revenue comes out to little less than $2 a day. The electricity necessary to deliver 65 TH from these three machines come to about 1350 W (remember, at least *one* of those terahashes are from the very inefficient, but small, Braiins Mini Miner). Extrapolating out that usage, my heating *from these machines* — I, unfortunately, have a large one in the bedroom that I run sparsely at night and another in the bathroom — **costs me $5.62 a day for a daily loss of around $3.60.**

…but that’s *completely* the wrong way of thinking about mining bitcoin at home.

***

## Returns Everywhere: *Diminishing* Returns!

If you think miner profitability for two seconds, you realize that profitable mining *at residential rates* couldn’t possibly have made sense in the first place. As I wrote in the Nordic Node this summer (https://stacker.news/items/1530104)

> If a top-of-the-line machine from a few miner generations ago, optimized for use in the home (i.e., durable and *quiiiieeet*) were profitable on residential power rates, *you’d just scrap the guardrails and run it commercially for profit*.

Remember Tyler Stevens and Dylan Seib from [Exergy](https://www.exergyheat.com/) in their “[Bitcoin Home Mining Playbook](https://www.tftc.io/bitcoin-home-mining-playbook-exergy)” booklet, released together with TFTC: **your mining operation just has to be** [**useful**](https://fountain.fm/episode/BuLYdGnAhY8JjhSNe6Bw?t=344)**.** (https://stacker.news/items/1426924, https://stacker.news/items/1542390)

**> “You’re already paying for electricity to make heat. A miner converts the same electricity to the same heat and earns Bitcoin while it does. The electricity cost is identical.”**

The first heater I got — purchased with declining and ever-more worthless sats roughly at the peak of the 2025 euphoria — straight out replaced my 1500W electrical space heater. I wasn’t running that one on maximum around the clock (especially not on sunny spring and summer days), and unfortunately never kept good track of its usage. If I were to guess, I’d say something like 900W at 16 hours a day in winter, maybe 500W at 6 hours a day on average across summer months.

The price _insensitivity_ of this is what makes the home miners so competitive (well, "competitive") vs industrial corporate, AI-exposed miners. I don't *have* to pass a profit-and-loss test... I just have to be useful. And the waste heat (a problem for most industrial activities) is a benefit for me, *indeed the main point!*

That adds up to about **3,500 kWh in a typical year**. Add in the other electrical heaters in my house, and we’d probs be looking at some 5,000 kWh for annual heating purposes. (This estimate is probably lowballing *things quite a lot* because for the [three months I measured back in the spring](https://stacker.news/items/1466211), the *total household usage* was about 4,000 kWh; OK fine, light, coffee, fridge and the literal oven might account for quite a bit of that.)

Running the Ofen 2 at a weighted average of 494W (minus vacations/time away from house, downtime on extremely sunny and warm summer days etc.), and I’m probably looking at north of 4,000 kWh in a year for this machine alone.

With this *second* Ofen entering my home, the new one taking on the heavy heating duties of the old one, the first one is relegated to less important tasks. *Diminishing returns; Austrian econ and ordinal utility,* [*Böhm-Bawerk’s horses*](https://mises.org/mises-wire/why-austrians-stress-ordinal-utility) *etc*.
Meaning: The *Ofen 2* won’t burn 4,000 kWh this year... though its faster, nimbler sibling might: extrapolating its current 659W use (on Two) *for the entire year* gives me 5,772 kWh.

It’s not quite the dead of winter yet, and I’ve already permanently retired the two other small wall-attached heaters I used (500W and 400W respectively) — though never run at full blast, except for during the worst storms and cold, dark winter days. Also, the Ofen 2 now permanently sits in the office, and I’ve already turned it off a few hours a day on hot days (Including today). Presumably, its wonderful 90%+ uptime is gonna fall off *markedly* going forward… judging from the last two weeks, and adjusting for winter-summer, **all-year usage uptime might be about 50%**.
(Once I get my distribution company to install a smart meter https://stacker.news/items/1601880 and I bag a third off my rate during night hours, I might even *increase* my use a bit...)

**First**, then, I should consider the higher efficiency of the new machine. The *bulk* of my house’s heating will now happen at ^18 J/TH instead of ^20.5, routinely generating 30-40-50 TH/s instead of 20-30 TH/s as before. Probably not a kWh savings, but definitely a *sats* boost.

**Second**, with the other low-use heaters gone, the Ofen 2 is now displacing about 2,000 kWh a year… incidentally, what my previous use *times* 50% uptime would consume, meaning the \~1,300 sats a day attributable to *it* is a pure Pareto optimal improvement.

**Third**, quality-of-life adjustments. I definitely kept rooms I wasn’t using (e.g., the office during night) unheated before. Now I just let the Ofen 2 keep it warm all the time… *incredibly* nice to walk into the office in the morning and *not* be chilly. And, honestly, the same probably goes for the living room (where the Ofen 3 lives), and I’m keeping the ambient temperature higher than before.

**I don’t have a good final-figure/TL;DR conclusion here.** Going off vibes and feelz from the last two weeks: when I got the Ofen 2 last year, it *definitely reduced the total electricity use* compared to what I had been using. With the Ofen 3 Pro routinely using quite a bit more (800-900 W on higher levels or 650 on Two, versus Ofen 2’s 500-700W on those same levels), and the Ofen 2 displacing less than it will (probably) consume, I might actually start using *more* kilowatt-hours rather than fewer.

More heat, more sats, more fiat bills.

The upside of that is a) more sats, and b) better quality of life since I foresee keeping my home at a warmer temperature than I did before … and c) *looks better*! ( d) *I feel like a cool heatpunk...?)*

## The Sats Carry Trade: Financialization Mania

It’s the 21st century, and we live under fiat, so the standard rule applies: **All that which can be financialized, *must be* financialized.**

You could think of the electricity-for-sats trade as a *BN;PL scheme* for Bitcoiners…

Because the electricity I burn for sats *today —* some 28 kWh or so; it was warm and calm today — pays me perhaps 2,500 sats *tomorrow morning* (thanks to the wonders of FPPS pools…). But the expense gets recorded by my electricity and distribution companies for November, with the associated fiat invoice due Jan 1 and Jan 7, respectively.

That gets me about 6 weeks of free float. (If I were more degenerate about this, which I *obviously* am, I’d hurl the proceeds into Predyx and buy a safe Nothing Ever Happens  https://stacker.news/items/1602534 short-dated contract for another \~5% return.) Yes, I found the long-awaited answer to *Where does the yield come from?!*

By the logic of time-value-of-money or basic finance, earlier is better. Also, as I wrote in a hopelessly optimistic and bullish [Bitcoin Magazine article years ago](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/culture/dca-effective-going-all-in-on-bitcoin),

> Investing on top of a structurally upward-moving trajectory, a positive-sum game, tilts the stakes in **favor of getting in earlier** (once again, ‘time *in* the market…’).”

Meaning: the sats can appreciate between the moment I earn them and the due date of the fiat liability that created them. Financial fiat alchemy is *on*!

Further, if I swap some of these juicy sats for fiat at a premium to market price, e.g., via peer-to-peer exchanges with a premium https://stacker.news/items/1559053, I can usually bag another couple of percentage points. 
(For all the feds who may or may not be reading, this is of course *totally hypothetical and for illustrative purposes only; not legal or financial advice.*)

In recent years and months, this carry trade hasn’t been an unmitigated *benefit*, with the BTC/USD exchange rate repeatedly dropping like a stone. Still, over time and given that our strong belief in an orange future is correct — certainly something you need to have as a miner/hasher, since the financial benefit of a hashing machine lies mostly in the (far-off) *future* c(h)ash flow it brings — this *should* work out in my favor. Eventually.

## Worth it?

**Yes**. 

I mean, a home miner isn’t a financial decision of the type “I buy this, I’ll make x profit monthly, and by \[purchasing price divided by x] in the future I will have economically paid it off.”

You should start with your own circumstances; assess your own heating needs and how you’re fulfilling those today; what your residential rates are, your potential uptime, and whether there’s something **useful** you can do with the (waste) heat — e.g., heat a sauna or outdoor pool. *Noise?* And also, obviously, what do you think the future of hashprice is? Bitcoin exchange rate? The premium you place on non-KYC sats, or learning about the energy/mining side of things.  

The questions never end. And that is, at least in part, why heatpunkery is so exciting!

*Happy hashing, friends!*

items.title: Yuval Harari on AI: Money, Stocks, and Bonds as Shared Trust (X, Harari)
items.text:
Our friend Tomer Strolight shared this talk by Yuval Harari on the AI revolution and what it means. (Apperently given at the Milan Leadership Forum 2026, Sept 30)

Harari, a mid-level but popular midwit, had quite a lot of interesting things to say about the history of banks and money in this recent lecture about AI (tl;dr: *LANGUAGE is amazing*)

Plenty of Christianity in there, shared myths and the collective and cooperative functioning of human societies... but I thought to illustrate/shout out the money and finance connection therein:

* Paul Seabright's book (https://stacker.news/items/1429046), [*The Company of Strangers: A Natural History of Economic Life*](https://link.amazon/B0g1pqzos) has this background too: what does money *do* in society https://stacker.news/items/780358
* I opened my "On Monetary Premia" essay (https://stacker.news/items/830458) on this feature, which I still believe is the best, most insightful thing I ever wrote
* and it's been top of mind recently: what are we *supposed to do* (https://stacker.news/items/1620193) when those assets don't do their jobs anymore

***

Anyway, here's the critical bit:

> Bureaucracies are the underappreciated heroes of history…

...ugh, makes me throw up in my mouth and I *certainly* think we can do a lot of human stuff without them. Anyway, his point is that their job = "to build trust between strangers”

> what banks do is to build trust between strangers, so that millions of people can pool their resources and talents together, such as constructing towers and spaceships.
>
> **The financial history of the world** is the history of humans inventing more and more sophisticated ways to build trust between strangers. Money is a bridge of trust. So also are bonds and stocks and ETFs and the entire market.

*the raw material from which money is made and banks operate? “A story made from words”*

## AGENCY and TRUST

We used to subserve or organize natural environment or pigs and horses under our bureaucracies: laws, finance, ownership (https://stacker.news/items/1565551) etc. "We invented money and banks and used them to buy and sell cows, but the cows themselves could not open a bank account or invest money in the stock exchange..."
> we invented laws and courts and regulations about horses, but the horses themselves could not hire a lawyer to argue a law to a judge. We invented religious rules and prohibitions regarding pigs but the pigs themselves could not read the Bible and challenge the interpretations of rabbis and priests.

> **"AIs are hacking the code of human civilization... we are seeing *language* coming to life!"**
> Just as cows and chickens don't understand the human financial system that controls their lives, we humans will not be able to understand the new AI systems that will control _our_ lives. 

Tomer thought the point about time or time use https://stacker.news/items/1591951 at the end critical, but I found the collab/money/financial control over real stuff more exciting.

"The real currency of life is time: time to rest, time to meditate"
---


---

**Stupid remark about chess in there, too...** saying that _AI_ reinvented chess and play better than humans now. That's false... _the consumer, all-purpose AIs we all know (and love/hate)_ are pretty bad at chess still. (Getting better, but even I would probably beat most of them most of the time). Their predecessors, LLMs, specifically trained on and guided on the limited ruleset of chess -- what we now call "chess engines", Stockfish, Leela etc -- were the wombs and early-stage trials. E.g., ***Google DeepMind*** and AlphaZero etc.

## Announcements

Welcome to the newsletter. Thanks to everyone who participated in this week's double awards contest. I will do them more often if there is enough participation. @denlillaapan 's product review took top honors. I believe this is a first, but I hope there are more to come.

Have a good week!

Logo design by @plebpoet
Link to last week's newsletter: [Bitcoin Beginners Newsletter #125](https://stacker.news/items/1618049/r/siggy47)

## Top 5 Posts Of The Week

There will be a zap award for the top 5 posts weekly. It will be broken down as follows:

1. 2000 sats
2. 500 sats
3. 500 sats
4. 500 sats
5. 500 sats

I choose the top 5 posts each week based on sats, engagement, and overall quality. The cut off time is 9:00am EST (1300GMT) Friday morning. I will post the top 5 winners shortly after 9:00am every Friday morning.

I reserve the right to not award any sats for the week. I also reserve the right to deny sat awards to bare link posts. I recognize that link posts can be valuable, so I will only exercise discretion for low quality links that garner few sats or engagement from stackers.

1. 🥇 2000 sats - [Burning Electricity for Yet More Sats: 21 Energy and their new Ofen 3 Pro](https://stacker.news/items/1619836/r/siggy47) by @denlillaapan
2. 🥈 500 sats - [How to use your first s9 / Why I bought a trunk-load of broken, out of date, s9s](https://stacker.news/items/1618150/r/siggy47) by @jasonb

## Learning Resources

### Start Here

- [The White Paper](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf) - Everyone knows about the white paper, but have you read it?

- [Get On BTC](https://getonbtc.com/) - Five foundational lessons covering money, ownership, getting started, pitfalls to avoid, and FAQs. Includes wallet recommendations and an AI chatbot for questions. Great starting point for true beginners.

- [Jameson Lopp's Getting Started With Bitcoin](https://www.lopp.net/bitcoin-information/getting-started.html) - Lopp's [website](https://www.lopp.net/articles.html) is an incredible resource for people interested in learning about bitcoin at any level. For those who can do without Lopp's shitcoinery, here is a curated [fork](https://btcmaxis.com/) of the site.

- [Learn Me A Bitcoin](https://learnmeabitcoin.com/) - Greg Walker explains bitcoin in a way that everyone can understand.

### Go Deeper

- [DarthCoin Guides](https://darth-coin.github.io/) - Excellent step by step instruction for those learning about nodes, particular wallets, and just about everything else in the ecosystem.

- [Lightning Network Documents](https://lightning.network/docs/) - Good complement to the white paper.

- [Opcode Explained](https://opcodeexplained.com/) - Documenting bitcoin opcodes, one at a time.

### Directories

- [Why Bitcoin Only](https://whybitcoinonly.com/) - This is a massive trove of links, where you can find just about anything you're looking for. It's also fun to browse around.

- [Bitcoin Apps Ecosystem 26.03.08](https://stacker.news/items/1449907/r/siggy47) by @R4DENT0R - A comprehensive ecosystem map. The most recent version is from March 2026, so some entries may be out of date, but beginners and experienced bitcoiners alike will benefit from checking it out.

items.title: The NEETS are Back: Britain's Failed Welfare State (WSJ, Editorial Board)
items.text:
We already know the old world is screwed. *Europooreans* isn't even a funny term anymore. https://stacker.news/items/1560586, https://stacker.news/items/1598264

We also know that *Britain specifically* is double-screwed... no growth industries (but porn and football, https://stacker.news/items/1495638, https://stacker.news/items/1006594), an oversized government, and a welfare state shoving over a million grown-ups into a complete dependency trap.

## The Redcoats Are Just Fucked, basically.

> Britain has a crisis of unemployed young people caused by welfare-state failures, and the government finances are in disarray. So the obvious solution is . . . more entitlements for the young? Behold Europe’s social-welfare meltdown in a nutshell. Nearly a million young adults in Britain aren’t working, pursuing higher education or in job training.

![](https://m.stacker.news/168628)

There was **a new report released** by, not a crazy market capitalist ruthless egghead but by "a respected Labour expert on social welfare," concluding, *shockingly*:

## "youth joblessness has risen as government policies made hiring young people more expensive and generous disability benefits made not working easier."

*Knock me down with a feather...* any econ 101 textbook could have told you as much.

> One in eight Britons younger than 25 are idle. Most have never held a job and aren’t looking for one. Many support themselves with disability-linked welfare benefits, primarily for vaguely defined or overdiagnosed behavioral or mental-health conditions such as anxiety, depression, ADHD or autism

It's all fake, and they're all leeches https://stacker.news/items/1592172... again, totally shocking outcome:

> Aggressive increases to the minimum wage in recent years are another major culprit, and a central fact in this report is that wage costs for an 18- to 20-year-old employee have risen 65% in the past five years. Increases in the payroll tax (called “national insurance”), split between employees and employers, have hit industries such as hospitality and retail that have thin profit margins and employ young people.

***

The real tragedy, aside from taxing productive people in order to ruin the social and economic prospects for the unproductive, is that *it's not good for the NEETs either!*

You'd think it's all chill and weed and GTA 6, but alas... not great. We need purpose and meaning, browskies.

> Worse, young people who don’t work lose the opportunity to develop skills, and the economy loses productivity. Dependency weighs on these young welfare beneficiaries, fostering frustration over “lost opportunities, lost earnings, lost confidence and lost purpose,” Mr. Milburn writes. His report exposes a troubling hopelessness among the country’s unemployed youth. **Alas, the Milburn report also exposes how hard it is to fix any of this.**

Yeah, obvs disagree with that... *You can just abolish stuff*, starting with benefits to the boomers -- because, honestly, FUCK. THEM. and take their stuff. https://stacker.news/items/1621298, https://stacker.news/items/1521908, https://stacker.news/items/1528521, https://stacker.news/items/1614018

...then the report goes, uh, *weird* to say the least:

> Mr. Milburn oddly doesn’t recommend immediately cutting payroll taxes, which he estimates would require the government to forgo £5 billion in revenue per year. He instead proposes spending even more, such as £5.8 billion ($7.6 billion) in annual government “investment” in youth productivity by fiscal 2036-37. **He calls for some £1.1 billion a year for hiring, wage and retention subsidies for employers. There’s no evidence these programs will work, since nothing like them ever has.**

## "to make up for the harm from subsidies and mandates that punish work, Mr. Milburn wants more subsidies and mandates to coax the young to work."

**Makes sense. MOAR COWBELL!**

![](https://m.stacker.news/168633)

***

items.title: Chess World Championship: Samba in Braziiiiil
items.text:
OK, fine... I'll stop the slacking https://stacker.news/items/1621690 -- also, we have a rest day today, with Game 4 on Saturday so might as well post something. 

We had a London in Game 2 (https://stacker.news/items/1621013) and an innovative and interesting Berlin endgame in Game 1 (https://stacker.news/items/1620451)...

## Today, Sindarov with the white pieces again went for the Spanish, heading toward his prep in the Berlin.

...but *Gukesh* surprised us by playing a SUPER RARE sideline called the **Rio de Janeiro variation of the Spanish**. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruy_Lopez#:~:text=There%20are%20also%20a%20number%20of%20sidelines%20that%20Black%20can%20also%20play%20which%20avoid%20the%20endgame.%20These%20include%205...Be7%2C%20the%20Rio%20de%20Janeiro%20Variation) says that it's a way to "avoid the endgame.") I've never heard of it... which, of course doesn't say much: I'm a schmuck. https://stacker.news/items/1598241

The tables were completely turned, with *Sindarov* massively down on the clock, Gukesh knowing everything and blitzing out moves (all the way up to move \~20-ish). ***Crazy***. Some excitement and weird positions in the middlegame, but it all fiddled out into an opposite-color bishop endgame.

...as always, chess is a draw if both players play perfectly. We got an accuracy score *even higher* than in Game 2
![](https://m.stacker.news/168638)

***

## playing chess in the 21st century:

"Wow, Gukesh is the first to deviate," said Peter Svidler on the livestream, genuinely surprised!

* "...as a surprise weapon for one game, it's *excellent*!"
* "similar in spirit to the Berlin, despite the queens remaining on"
* "Javokhir has the better version of this 0.00 position"

And **this is elite, high-level chess with long time controls.** You have two extremely well-prepared dudes (assisted by large teams of seconds and researchers) coming into a head-to-head 14-game match in *long af* time controls. Everybody knows everything, has studied every line more or less... to get an advantage and some winning chances, you *have to take some obscure paths*, often even objectively losing: going down a pawn, horrible and ugly structure. 

![](https://m.stacker.news/168639)

Yesterday, we *almost* got triple pawns... unfortunately, Sindarov didn't play Qxc4 to create that nice kebab-stack of pawns on the c-file, but instead just attacked the queen with a pawn (b3), overprotecting the knight. **You take meeee, bitch**... which Gukesh did in the game. 

*Interesting observation, also*: as black, you can't just take that free c pawn... and then *also* the b pawn after the queen is attacked by the rooks. Putting *that* position on the board, we get a +0.7 evaluation *even though black has just gobbled two pawns*. 

![](https://m.stacker.news/168640)

queen *doesn't get trapped*, it's just bad long-term/positional (*I guess*...?). And honestly, black just won't be able to defend those two doubled pawns on the c-file. 

***

Yeah, I wrote this playing the old-school "Samba" song on repeat.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fhHKYR-v0UE

items.title: Tether Fun Unbelievable Details - Part VII
items.text:
*This is part of a larger series on the history of Tether. Part I (*https://stacker.news/items/1042943*), Part II (*https://stacker.news/items/1059310*), Part III (*https://stacker.news/items/1115791*), Part IV (*https://stacker.news/items/1410689/*), Part V (*https://stacker.news/items/1613156*), Part VI (https://stacker.news/items/1617443)*

# 20 THE GENIUS ACT

20.1   The primary version of the GENIUS Act (Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act) of 2025 [is introduced](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/bills/119/s919/text/is) in the US Senate by Bill Hagerty, Cynthia Lummis, Kirsten Gillibrand, and Tim Scott on 10 March 2025.

20.11   Also on this day: "GM, back to Washington DC today" [-Paolo Ardoino](https://x.com/paoloardoino/status/1899074589868581364)

20.12   An earlier version of the bill was [first introduced](https://www.cov.com/en/news-and-insights/insights/2025/02/seven-things-to-know-about-the-federal-stablecoin-bill-the-genius-act) on 4 February 2025.

20.121   This was based on draft legislation Bill Hagerty [released](https://www.hagerty.senate.gov/press-releases/2024/10/10/hagerty-releases-discussion-draft-of-comprehensive-stablecoin-legislation/) on 10 October 2024.

20.122   "Stablecoins have the potential not only to enhance transactions and payment systems, but also to help create new demand for U.S. Treasuries as we work to address our unsustainable deficit," [said Senator Hagerty](https://www.hagerty.senate.gov/press-releases/2024/10/10/hagerty-releases-discussion-draft-of-comprehensive-stablecoin-legislation/). "For too long, these benefits and the broader promise of stablecoins have been hindered by the lack of clear regulations. My draft legislation provides much-needed clarity, putting in place the legal framework necessary to unlock this technology’s full potential for the benefit of Americans."

20.2   The month before, on 13 September 2024, Tether [announced](https://tether.io/news/industry-leader-jesse-spiro-joins-tether-as-head-of-government-affairs/) that they were hiring Jesse Spiro as Head of Government Affairs.

20.21   On 26 February 2025, Jesse Spiro [registers](https://lda.gov/filings/public/filing/6d351923-49fd-4662-b017-c3d9150a696f/print/) Jucundus Business Services LLC as a organization/lobbying firm lobbying on behalf Tether Holdings, S.A. de C.V. and Giancarlo Devasini, c/o SHRM Trustees BVI Limited

20.211   On a 21 April 2025 Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995 Lobbying Report, Jesse Spiro [reports](https://lda.gov/filings/public/filing/582b5e28-638b-4083-abaf-dca18ce9b4a6/print/) $40,000 of lobbying income for Jucundus Business Services LLC specifying activity related to "legislative and regulatory policies related to cryptocurrency" and "S. 394, GENIUS Act of 2025" and "H.R. 2392, STABLE Act of 2025"

20.212   Jesse Spiro list his [contact email](https://lda.gov/filings/public/filing/582b5e28-638b-4083-abaf-dca18ce9b4a6/print/) as [jesse.spiro@tether.to](mailto:jesse.spiro@tether.to)

20.22   "I think that Genius Act is a step in the right direction." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.221   "it creates a strong framework for domestic stablecoins, as well as foreign stablecoins like USDT that could find in their ability to meet their requirements through comparable regimes." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.222   "the Genius Act creates a very, very high bar for everyone. That's the thing that I think I like the most, and it's very fair. In a sense that it creates a very high bar when it comes to AML and compliance. Yesterday, there was a huge news of Tether collaborating with the Department of Justice. Tether was able, with its own means, almost one year and a half ago at this point, to identify through its monitoring technology. We built, I think, the most amazing technology for monitoring our secondary markets in the blockchain ecosystem when it comes to stable coins and specific USDT. We were able to identify a big battery scheme and when we did that, we immediately notified the law enforcement, i.e. the DOJ, and they agreed with our analysis. We proceed to the freezing and now basically the DOJ is in the process of receiving this money and working on restitution." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.223   "We collaborated with more than 250 law enforcement agencies across more than 55 different countries." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.224   "Tether has in this moment as a group equity has around $176 billion in front of the $155 billion in market cap of the stable coin. And precisely, we keep just on top of the single reserves of the stablecoin, of the 100% of reserves of the USDT stablecoin, we keep around $6 billion in excess, right? Compared to the standard banking system that usually goes in fractional reserve up to 90%. So they keep only 10% of liquid assets. Tether has like 100 and something percent, like 105 percent of liquid assets as reserves of the stable coin. On top of that, we have another 15 billion dollars as a group equity to add." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.225   "Remember 2023 when you know our major competitor almost died because of Silicon Valley Bank and Silvergate signature, all targeted by the Operation Choke Point 2.0, but nevertheless almost killed our competitor." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.226   "But you know I just I just want to applaud the the efforts that have been done by by Senator Hagerty, Lummis and all the others David Sacks, Bo Hines." [-Paolo Ardoino on *Bankless*](https://banklesscom.beehiiv.com/p/the-stablecoin-king-tether-ceo-paolo-ardoino)

20.23   "I view our role, specifically my office, as being like an administrator and/or sherpa between White House policy, industry, interagency activity and what's happening on Capitol Hill" [-Bo Hines](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2025-04-04-three-months-in-bo-hines-on-quarterbacking-the-white-houses-crypto-strategy-349632)

20.231   "We created them (a bitcoin reserve and crypto stockpile) separately for a reason and that reason is because bitcoin is unique. Bitcoin is the grandfather." [-Bo Hines](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2025-04-04-three-months-in-bo-hines-on-quarterbacking-the-white-houses-crypto-strategy-349632)

20.232   In response to a Coindesk question about how much Bitcoin should be in the US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, Bo Hines [says](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-bitcoin-reserve-plans-continue-donald-trump-bo-hines) "As much as we can possibly get."

20.24   "In order for their stablecoins to trade among U.S. users, under the latest version, foreign stablecoin issuers will have their nation's regulatory regime assessed by the Treasury and other banking regulators for comparability with the U.S." [-Brady Dale, "Latest Senate stablecoin bill addresses foreign issuers, national security safeguards" *Axios*](https://archive.is/RqM1x)

20.241   "The Trump administration, for example, could strike a reciprocity agreement with the Bukele regime in El Salvador, where Tether is based, allowing Tether full access to the U.S. market while sidestepping the requirements of the bill." [-Democratic Staff of the Senate Banking Committee Outline Critical Ammendments to Fix *The GENIUS Act*](https://www.banking.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/genius_act_analysis_6925.pdf)

20.242   "Similarly, the OCC is not providing a safe harbor for foreign affiliates that operate under a comparable regime because these are determinations of the Department of the Treasury that have yet to be made." [-Federal Register](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-23/html/2026-21706.htm)

20.25   "Hines, who President Donald Trump hired as executive director of the Presidential Council of Advisers for Digital Assets, told CoinDesk in an interview that the procedures are being ironed out to move legislation on regulating stablecoin issuers, and the crypto advocates in the White House and Congress will quickly pivot to the bigger bill that will set a full regulatory regime for U.S. crypto markets." [-Jesse Hamilton, "Trump's Crypto Sherpa Bo Hines Says Crypto Legislation on Target for Quick Completion" *CoinDesk* 30 April 2025](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512151544/https://www.coindesk.com/consensus-toronto-2025-coverage/2025/04/30/trumps-crypto-sherpa-bo-hines-says-crypto-legislation-on-target-for-quick-completion)

20.251   "We view bitcoin as digital gold, and we want to accumulate as much as we can." [-Bo Hines](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512151544/https://www.coindesk.com/consensus-toronto-2025-coverage/2025/04/30/trumps-crypto-sherpa-bo-hines-says-crypto-legislation-on-target-for-quick-completion)

20.252   "The then-29-year-old White House aide, a North Carolina entrepreneur and crypto investor who ran unsuccessful congressional campaigns as a Republican in 2022 and 2024, became the administration’s self-described “bully” on the bill. As negotiations neared the finish line, Hines said that a provision Tether wanted was a “red line” for the White House, according to three other people familiar with the matter." [-Anthony Cormier, David Kocieniewski, and Annie Massa, "How Tether Benefited as Trump Insiders Shaped First US Crypto Law" *Bloomberg* 22 July 2026](https://archive.is/agHnj)

20.253   "In negotiations, he told people that Tether was important to the White House and Republicans should stand firm. Keeping the three-year grace period was a “red line,” Hines said, according to three people familiar with his conversations." [-Anthony Cormier, David Kocieniewski, and Annie Massa, "How Tether Benefited as Trump Insiders Shaped First US Crypto Law" *Bloomberg* 22 July 2026](https://archive.is/agHnj)

20.26   A 10 March 2025 version of the GENIUS Act requires that US digital-asset service providers only offer qualifying stablecoins (ie not USDT) within 18 months of the bill's passage, however by 1 May, this grace-period was extended to three years.

20.261   "In general.--Except as provided in subsection (c) and section 18, beginning on the date that is 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, it shall be unlawful for any digital asset service provider to offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States, unless the payment stablecoin is issued by a permitted payment stablecoin issuer." [-S. 1582 "A Bill To provide for the regulation and of payment stablecoins, and for other purposes"](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s1582pcs/html/BILLS-119s1582pcs.htm)

20.27   On 17 June 2025, The GENIUS Act (P.L. 119-27) [is passed](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R49351.html#_Toc240544941) on a final vote of 68-30 by the Senate

20.28   On 17 July 2025, it [is passed](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R49351.html#_Toc240544941) by the House 308-122 without amendment.

20.29   President Donald Trump [signs](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/07/the-president-signed-into-law-s-1582/) the GENIUS Act into law on 18 July 2025.

20.3   "Where's Bo Hines?" [-Donald Trump, during the signing of the GENIUS Act](https://archive.is/nfiDU#selection-2513.69-2513.89)

20.31   22 December 2024 Trump [appoints](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/statement-president-elect-donald-j-trump-announcing-science-and-technology-team) Bo Hines to be Executive Director of the Presidential Council of Advisers for Digital Assets.

20.311   "...Additionally, Bo Hines will be the Executive Director of the Presidential Council of Advisers for Digital Assets (the "Crypto Council"), a new advisory group composed of luminaries from the Crypto industry, and chaired by our Crypto Czar, David Sacks. Bo is a graduate of Yale University, and Wake Forest University Law School. In his new role, Bo will work with David to foster innovation and growth in the digital assets space, while ensuring industry leaders have the resources they need to succeed. Together, they will create an environment where this industry can flourish, and remain a cornerstone of our Nation's technological advancement." [-Donald Trump](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/113698639577293090)

20.312   Hines was a "two-time Republican congressional candidate, who had never held a formal business role in the tight-knit crypto sector" [-Jessica Matthews and Leo Schwartz, "Trump's senior crypto advisor donated $1M in campaign advertisements to top Trump super PAC one week before election" *Fortune* 14 April 2026](https://fortune.com/2025/04/14/trump-senior-crypto-advisor-donated-1m-campaign-advertisements-maga-super-pac-week-before-election/)

20.313   "Four years after he graduated from Yale, Hines ran for the House in a North Carolina district in the Raleigh area with an endorsement from Trump, making it to the general election before he lost in 2022." [-Jessica Matthews and Leo Schwartz, "Trump's senior crypto advisor donated $1M in campaign advertisements to top Trump super PAC one week before election" *Fortune* 14 April 2026](https://fortune.com/2025/04/14/trump-senior-crypto-advisor-donated-1m-campaign-advertisements-maga-super-pac-week-before-election/)

20.314   "Two years later, in 2024, he lost in the primary in a different district." [-Jessica Matthews and Leo Schwartz, "Trump's senior crypto advisor donated $1M in campaign advertisements to top Trump super PAC one week before election" *Fortune* 14 April 2026](https://fortune.com/2025/04/14/trump-senior-crypto-advisor-donated-1m-campaign-advertisements-maga-super-pac-week-before-election/)

20.32   "Prior to politics Hines played college football as a wide receiver for North Carolina State and Yale. He received a law degree from Wake Forest University in 2022, and is 29 years old." [-Unchained Crypto](https://unchainedcrypto.beehiiv.com/p/who-will-be-on-the-crypto-council)

20.321   "Hines became interested in crypto when he played football in the 2014 Bitcoin St. Petersburg Bowl for North Carolina State during his freshman year in college. items.title: Acemoglu Wants Pro-Worker AIs (FT, Daron Acemoglu)
items.text:
*Gimme some of that "pro-worker AI", sir!*

![](https://m.stacker.news/168066)

The [economist who forgot economics](https://www.econlib.org/the-economist-who-forgot-economics) is out here talking, if not bullshit than at *least* some sort of shit. 

> The impressive victory of Democrats in the midterms is a lifeline for US democracy. But the challenges ahead are formidable. Democrats remain divided, with so-called progressives and moderates increasingly critical of each other.  **The standard narrative here misses the big picture.**

OK, cool; enlighten us, oh you shiny Nobel Prize-winning elite economist.

Apparently, the story goes that *moderate* Democrats are more economically literate, while it's the progressives who mess about with radical nonsense ideas.

## "alas, the ideas that progressives advocate are no match for the transformations impacting our economy. Rather than being too bold, progressives, also, are too timid."

**4 types of progressive policies we need**

1. "**Ensuring affordability**": yeah, amazing.

> such as city-owned grocery stores or free bus services in New York. Slightly lower grocery bills will not change the fact that about half the US population has seen very little gain in their (pre-tax) real incomes since around 1980.

oh yeah, PREACH! https://stacker.news/items/1608876 https://stacker.news/items/1599758

2. **"policies to push for higher wages" oh great**
   Force companies to share AI profits with workers (yes, they do; it's called equity compensation, of which there has been a ton https://stacker.news/items/1619212; or just generally *wages*, https://stacker.news/items/1457057, https://stacker.news/items/1601547, so what's your point?)

> If AI continues to go in the direction of automation, any policy that increases wages would only further motivate employers to automate more — since incentives to do so are proportional to the labour costs that companies would save.

Sure yeah, that's a pickle.

3. **"some progressives have proposed pausing frontier AI or halting data centre construction."**

Have fun with that. *Life finds a way,* and also, NIMBY has never achieved anything good in human history, has it?

4. **"we could try to deal with inequality by increasing taxes and redistribution."**

Sure yeah, cool, that's a *great* way to go about things. Moar cowbell, gimme gimme gimme extra gov violence!!

> Ideas based on universal basic income (UBI) are particularly popular among some progressives. But UBI is defeatist, giving up on the aspiration to build a society in which people can use their talents. It is also likely to create a two-tiered world in which those who control AI will have huge incomes and prestige, even if they pay high taxes. Those living off UBI would be viewed as “takers”, with much less social status.

I dunno... would UBI takers be *more* or *less* stigmatized than welfare takers? https://stacker.news/items/1593954, https://stacker.news/items/1603158, https://stacker.news/items/1602493 **what about the boomers??**

## "Fortunately, something more radical is available. We are just not discussing it at the moment"

AMAZING, let's go!

* AI might complement workers, making them more productive and richer (https://stacker.news/items/1618797)
* "Human cognition is clearly multimodal" OK fine, AI-written warning on that one. "AI models, meanwhile, excel at the things that humans cannot do." ish.

> If two things are different, the most natural way of using them is in a complementary way. So it should be with AI and humans. But here is the snag. Captivated by dreams of superintelligence, the industry is not pursuing this and, left to its own devices, it won’t. Progressive policy should recognise this reality and build institutions and norms to encourage pro-worker AI.

This bit I don't *quite* understand. **HOW?!**

> If an automation technology and humans have the same cost of performing a task, the current US tax code gives the company choosing automation a 20-25 per cent cost advantage. In principle, this is easy to fix. We can tax all income at the same rate, regardless of whether it is (often arbitrarily) labelled labour income or capital income.

Fine, sounds cool. I'm game.

...and then the article just fiddles out. Cool. **what tha hell is pro-worker AIs?!**

> Pro-worker AI is more radical than the policies progressives usually focus on. It asks us to do new things for a new age. This is the best kind of radicalism because it aims to help workers and it is feasible. What’s more, it may provide the best means of revitalising our crisis-ridden liberal democracy.

***

items.title: Bills Tiptoe by the Chiefs 13 -10: My Three Takeways
items.text:
Wow this is a game Buffalo usually loses but not tonight! Here are my three takeaways:

1. Short out to the Bills special teams. They were the difference in the game tonight. Tyler Bass hit FGs from 54 and 57 with the 57 being the game winning walk off kick. The punter Jake had a really good day. Pinning the Chiefs deep in their own territory was great in a game where the weather was so ugly. Then Buffalo Joe getting a tip on the punt and Dorch picking the ball up and getting 15 years was all great plays. They didn’t take any penalties on special teams. This unit was clearly better than KC’s and that was the difference in the game. 

2. Josh Allen was awful this game. Brady rode Cook all game long. 30 carries over 100 yards. With the weather being poor I don’t have an issue with Brady’s gameplay but when Spags started to dial up the blitz Brady and Josh had no answers. DJ and Kincaid were non factors. It would be easy to blame the weather but Mahomes was able to complete balls to Travis. This is what keeps me from saying that Josh Allen is the best QB in football. Throwing INTS in the red zone and just coming up with terrible games like this is why we haven’t won big yet. I hate to beat up the offense too much on a great win but we need more from Brady and Josh in big games like this. But I must say if Sean McDermott was coaching we probably lose this game. 

3. The refs were terrible tonight. They missed a lot of calls. It felt like they were trying to give the game to buffalo. The Rice call was a huge overturn. I thought he caught it but the booth replay overturned it. Just flags on top of flags. Travis was called for a meh pass interference and a meh holding call on Dawson Knox. Just wasn’t happen with the calls. We need the players  to determine these games not the refs. Now I see why folks started to hate the Chiefs normally THEY would get all of these calls.  But besides the refs the Bills defense did their job. Having Hooker is making an impact and I think the players are buying into Jim’s system. Overall I am happy with the Defense. 

This was a  tough game I am happy buffalo pulled it off. And now we have a 54% chance to get the one seed. Normally Bills Vs. Chiefs is our super bowl and then we have a let down. Hopefully with Brady that doesn’t happen.  Next week we get our revenge against New England

items.title: OpenBitcoin.com: A new bitcoin block explorer with guides tools and games
items.text:
I have been building a bitcoin block explorer and I feel it's good enough to show:

[https://openbitcoin.com](https://openbitcoin.com)

The site runs its own hardware, bitcoin node and address index. No third-party blockchain API used.

Inside the site:

- Explorer: blocks, transactions and addresses at root-level URLs. (very important, a feature I always wanted with other explorers, a quick easy way to query an address) For example you can type openbitcoin.com/block_number_here or openbitcoin.com/txid_here or openbitcoin.com/address_here to load the page instantly without visiting the site to use the search bar :)

- Node census (openbitcoin.com/nodes): reachable nodes counted by my own P2P crawler, 8,958 nodes from 92 countries last run.

- Rich list (openbitcoin.com/rich-list): top 10,000 addresses and balance distributions.

- Prices: spot price as a median of three exchanges, with a quick conversion tool on the front page.

- Tools: fee calculator, address validator, message verifier, QR generator, and key tools built to be downloaded and run offline.

- Guides: on confirmations, UTXOs, self-custody, stuck transactions and more. Newbie friendly.

- Games (openbitcoin.com/games): three arcade games built on real bitcoin mechanics, stack blocks, clear a mempool backlog, and a slot machine that plays the actual odds of guessing a private key.

The website is open source. What stays private is my server's operational layer.

Would appreciate any feedback, happy to contribute to the community.

items.title: Argentina bans its central bank from printing money for the government by law.
items.text:
## Argentina passed a law banning central bank money printing; the measure aims to curb inflation through fiscal reform

https://www.lanacion.com.ar/usa/argentina-bans-its-central-bank-from-printing-money-for-the-government-nid26112026/

Argentina’s Congress voted Thursday to bar the central bank from printing money to pay the government’s bills, enshrining in law a key pillar of President Javier Milei’s fight against the country’s notoriously high inflation.

Under the new charter, the central bank’s “primary and fundamental mission” will be to preserve the value of the peso — a goal Milei has pursued in office even though, as a candidate in 2023 , he promised to abolish the bank and replace the local currency with the U.S. dollar.

The 141-0 vote in the Chamber of Deputies, with 99 abstentions, comes days after preliminary figures showed Argentina had likely slipped into recession, less than a year before the libertarian economist seeks a second four-year term.

For generations, when Argentine governments spent more than they collected in taxes, they turned to the central bank to print pesos to fill the gap, fueling repeated currency crises and bouts of hyperinflation. The law puts an end to “91 years of plunder, expropriation, impunity and institutional decay,” Milei’s office said in a statement.

The new charter bars the bank from lending to any level of government or otherwise financing the Treasury. It also scraps the bank's employment and economic development goals added under former President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner , the Peronist opposition leader whose administrations leaned heavily on the central bank to fund unbridled spending.

But the law gives the monetary authority less protection than Milei sought. His original bill would have required a two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress to remove the bank’s governor, his appointee Santiago Bausili. The Senate watered down that clause, and the lower house lacked the votes Thursday to restore it. Now a president can replace the bank’s leadership with a simple Senate majority.

Milei has slashed public spending in the past three years, turning Argentina's chronic fiscal deficits into a surplus and helping cut annual inflation from nearly 300% in early 2024 to 33% last month.

Yet Milei has been reluctant to let the market set Argentina’s most important price: the exchange rate. The charter leaves currency controls in the bank’s hands and sets no clear rule for how it should respond to inflation.

Tight monetary policy has kept the peso strong, making Argentine goods expensive abroad just as factories face a flood of cheaper imports . Oil and gas exports have boomed while labor-intensive industries like manufacturing, retail and construction have struggled.

Argentina’s economy shrank an estimated 1.8% in the third quarter, after a 0.6% contraction in the second, according to official data released Tuesday. Two straight quarters of decline is the usual definition of a recession.

As Milei’s support slips in the polls, investors wary of a country infamous for defaulting on its debt nine times are weighing the possibility that the Peronists — the populist movement that has long dominated Argentine politics — could return to power and reverse his market-friendly reforms . The premium investors demand to hold Argentina’s bonds, a gauge of perceived default risk, has more than doubled since early August, according to JPMorgan.

Under growing pressure, Milei is now hoping to overhaul next year’s presidential race. The Senate on Thursday approved his bill to suspend the mandatory primaries, which the government argues waste public money on contests parties should run themselves. It now goes to the lower house for a vote.

Suspending the primaries, long a bellwether for the general election, would spare Milei an early verdict from voters — one that, if poor, could spook markets and sink the peso and his support with it.

Peronist leaders have balked at the move, which would force their fractured movement to negotiate a ticket behind closed doors or scramble to organize a primary of its own.

"Milei now wants to change the rules of democracy to improve his chances of reelection by cheating,” Buenos Aires province Gov. Axel Kicillof, a potential Peronist challenger to Milei, wrote on X.

items.title: An Intelligent Response to "Bitcoin Has Become Boring"
items.text:
I am responding to this article *here* by Roy.

https://stacker.news/items/1621381 [ ](https://blog.breez.technology/the-utility-of-bitcoin-moving-value-like-information-2513eae84676)

I only want to be polite and constructive... But some things needs to be said and I might as well say them. 

\----------------------------------- 

This is the dumbest article I have ever read.

The suits don't give a fuck about bitcoin. They don't even understand it, and generally speaking don't want to.

"Much of this scale is thanks to the millions of people who want to own bitcoin as part of their savings." Total incoherent nonsense. Bitcoin is in a serious bear market and the suits (much less the millions of savers) do you know what they want?

Stocks. They want stocks so the stocks can go up. They want the "AI trade" - NOT because they are actually interested in AI. Nope.

But because they think that *other people* will be interested in AI and by gosh the (AI sucker) is going up so buy and trade it.

I don't know anyone, not one person who meaningfully knows anything about bitcoin. I have known *some* who bought bitcoin that one time on coinbase... But self custody? No.

And lightning? Never heard of it.

I would say that bitcoin is even LESS mainstream than AI - actual AI like running AI locally and having an agent you maintain yourself. THAT is not common and bitcoin lightning is way less common than even that by a significant margin.

Furthermore... The vast majority of the people who "bought the ETF" have no fucking idea what they own. They don't know how bitcoin works or what its properties are... They just think its like another stock and when its doesn't "go up" they sell it and buy something else. That is generally speaking the limit of their knowledge.

And even worse bitcoin 'the commodity' has been mistakenly compared to unregistered securities like illegal securities-schemes xrp or solana or binance coin... Those things aren't even proof of work.

Or they are 'Cryptos' literally created by a for profit company without *any* disclosures in other words they are unregistered securities and ethically impossible.

If people don't understand what separates bitcoin from 'crypto', if they don't know that bitcoin is a product of energy, if they have *never* heard of lightning then bitcoin is NOT mainstream. Walk into your local convenicne store or grocery store - do they accept bitcoin?

NO. Does the cashier know anything about bitcoin? Does he have a 'lightning wallet?' No, he has no idea what you are talking about or what that is. Even if you said hey I'll tip you in lightning... They DO NOT know what that is. So how could bitcoin possibly be mainstream?

You know what many of those ETF people did? They sold their bitcoin "shares" and they bought micron. Or they bought nvidia. Or they bought nebius and coreweave and broadcom... And when Jensen slept with the spy do you know what they did (when he got "fired")?

They sold their shares. Because AI was "crashing." Did they actually use AI outside of trading? No. Maybe they used google AI search that one time... But did they use AI, pay for it, and engage with these models *which are really fucking intelligent?*

No way.

So how can we possibly say bitcoin is mainstream when they buy it even LESS than AI which they (to be honest) don't want to understand either! Or use!

ALL the Cryptos today, all of them including the stablecoins, add up to \~2 trillion dollars.

Nvidia alone (just for perspective) is worth over 3.5 trillion and that is just ONE stock. Apple is worth \~5 trillion, Microsoft is another 3.5, amazon is worth almost 3, and google is worth almost 3.5 trillion...

Those are single individual companies, all of them based in *one* country and they are individually worth multiples of bitcoin's market cap, *much less* added together, much less subtracting the 'Cryptos' ie unregistered securities which are illiquid and "worth" their tokens times ridiculous numbers (that somebody 'made up').

Bitcoin is a tiny asset *by comparison.*

Engage with commenters on any mainstream newspaper, even sophisticated ones like the wall street journal or the Washington post (pick your political bias) and the VAST majority don't know the difference between bitcoin and the trump coin. They think there are "thousands of Cryptos" (like the trump coin) and they are all the scams (like the trump coin) so they should be banned or heavily restricted.

They have NEVER read about lightning in bloomberg, it has NEVER been featured in the wall street journal, and many of the things they HAVE read are either wrong, grossly exaggerated, or have nothing to do with bitcoin and written by people who have a MAJOR agenda to sell.

Bitcoin is NOT mainstream.

If we WANT to make it mainstream we need to have a serious conversation about what it is, why its needed, and what will be the ultimate LONG TERM fate of fiats when their governments overspend at unsustainable levels. It is NOT sustainable and the governments MOST opposed to bitcoin (like France)? They are an economic basket case and they don't want anyone TO KNOW until it is TOO LATE. It will NOT be OK!

The LAST THING the "basket cases" like france want is bitcoin competing with their bonds or ANYTHING ELSE.

I could go on and on.

The bad news? Bitcoin is not mainstream. The good news? Bitcoin is not mainstream. Articles that say it is especially in this way are unconvincing, at best in a huge bubble, and at worst deluding themselves or others.

We need to be honest about what bitcoin is *today* and what it could become.
